requirements.text: The system shall accept a user-specified directory (or repository path) of Markdown files as input and recursively discover all `.md` files within it.
requirements.rationale: Directly supports G1 (ingest a folder of Markdown notes). Without file discovery the pipeline cannot begin.

requirements.text: The system shall parse each discovered Markdown file and generate a corresponding static HTML page that preserves the original Markdown formatting and structure (headings, lists, code blocks, images, emphasis, tables, etc.).
requirements.rationale: Supports G5 (preserve Markdown formatting) and G1 (generate a static website). Ensures content fidelity.

requirements.text: The generated output shall consist exclusively of static files (HTML, CSS, JS, and assets) that can be served by any static file server or opened locally, with no server-side runtime required for browsing, search, or backlinks.
requirements.rationale: Enforces CNS1 (static site constraint) and non-goal NG1 (no hosted SaaS/server-side DB).

requirements.text: The system shall build a client-side full-text search index at generation time and embed it in the static site so that users can search across all note contents and titles from the browser without a server.
requirements.rationale: Supports G2 (full-text search) and aligns with A3 (client-side search index) and CNS1.

requirements.text: Search results shall return relevant notes for a given query, with at least 90% of predefined representative queries returning the expected note within the top 10 results.
requirements.rationale: Directly maps to SM2 (search quality metric). Ensures search is practically useful.

requirements.text: The system shall extract tags from notes (at minimum from a YAML frontmatter field, with inline #tag support dependent on Q2 resolution) and generate navigable tag index pages or filters so users can browse notes by tag.
requirements.rationale: Supports G3 (tag-based browsing). Aligns with A4 (parseable tag representation) and SM3 (100% tag correctness).

requirements.text: 100% of notes containing tags in a dataset shall appear under their corresponding tag pages or filters in the generated site.
requirements.rationale: Directly maps to SM3 (tag extraction correctness metric). Ensures reliability of categorization.

requirements.text: The system shall detect forward links between notes (standard Markdown links and, pending Q1 resolution, wiki-link syntax) and render them as navigable hyperlinks in the generated HTML pages.
requirements.rationale: Supports G4 (detect and render forward links). Link detection is prerequisite for backlink computation.

requirements.text: The system shall compute backlinks for each note by analyzing all forward links across the note set and display a backlinks section on each note's page listing all notes that link to it.
requirements.rationale: Supports G4 (backlinks) and SM4 (100% backlink correctness). Core differentiating feature.

requirements.text: For a test set of interlinked notes, 100% of expected backlinks shall appear on their target note pages.
requirements.rationale: Directly maps to SM4 (backlink correctness metric).

requirements.text: The system shall be invocable via a command-line interface (CLI) that accepts at minimum the input directory path and an output directory path as arguments.
requirements.rationale: Supports A6 (user can run a CLI/build tool) and provides the primary user interaction model.

requirements.text: The build process shall complete without errors on a representative notes folder and produce a valid set of static files.
requirements.rationale: Directly maps to SM1 (build success metric). Baseline for all other features.

requirements.text: The generated site shall load and function correctly (navigation, search, backlinks, tags) in the latest stable versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge without JavaScript errors.
requirements.rationale: Directly maps to SM6 (cross-browser compatibility metric).

requirements.text: The system shall support CommonMark as the baseline Markdown flavor and additionally support GitHub-Flavored Markdown (GFM) extensions (tables, task lists, strikethrough). The exact flavor shall be finalized upon resolution of Q1.
requirements.rationale: Supports CNS2 (standard Markdown processing) and provides broad compatibility with common note-taking tools.

requirements.text: The system shall support wiki-link syntax (e.g., [[Note Title]]) for inter-note linking, in addition to standard Markdown links, with the exact syntax finalized upon resolution of Q1.
requirements.rationale: Wiki-links are the dominant convention in tools like Obsidian. Supports A2 (backlink derivation from wiki-links) and broadens usability.

requirements.text: The generated site shall include a site-wide navigation structure with at minimum an index/home page listing all notes and a tag index page listing all tags.
requirements.rationale: Improves discoverability and browsability of the note collection. Supports the overall goal of making notes navigable at scale.

requirements.text: On a representative dataset of 100+ notes, the static site generation shall complete within an agreed performance target (target TBD per Q3), and client-side search shall return results within 500ms.
requirements.rationale: Maps to SM7 (performance targets). Ensures the tool is practical for real-world note collections.

requirements.text: The system shall generate a table of contents (outline) for each note page based on its heading structure.
requirements.rationale: Addresses Q5 (note outline/TOC) and improves navigation within long notes.

requirements.text: The system shall support both YAML frontmatter tags and inline #tag syntax, with the option to configure which sources are used, pending resolution of Q2.
requirements.rationale: Maximizes compatibility with different note-taking conventions. Supports A4 and addresses Q2.

requirements.text: The CLI shall provide a watch mode that monitors the input directory for changes and incrementally regenerates affected pages.
requirements.rationale: Addresses Q4 (preferred build workflow). Significantly improves the authoring experience during development.

requirements.text: The generated site shall include an interactive graph view visualizing the link relationships between notes.
requirements.rationale: Addresses Q5 (graph view). Provides a powerful discovery mechanism but is not core to the primary goals.

requirements.text: The system shall support theming or customizable styling of the generated site via user-provided CSS or a theme configuration.
requirements.rationale: Addresses Q7 (themes/customizable styling). Enhances personalization but is secondary to core functionality.

requirements.text: Search shall support advanced features such as fuzzy matching, tag-based filtering of results, result highlighting, and sorting by relevance.
requirements.rationale: Addresses Q8 (specific search features). Improves search UX but basic full-text search satisfies the core goal.

requirements.text: The system shall support nested/hierarchical tags (e.g., `#parent/child`) and reflect the hierarchy in tag navigation.
requirements.rationale: Addresses the nested-tag aspect of Q2. Useful for users with complex taxonomies but not essential for initial delivery.
